meta.title: DiskMap Playground
meta.author: diskmap
meta.description: A fresh Nextcloud in the browser with the DiskMap app installed. Several accounts are seeded with files of different sizes so the instance-wide treemap has something to show.

steps.content:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--

  - SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
  -->
<info xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://apps.nextcloud.com/schema/apps/info.xsd">
    <id>diskmap</id>
    <name>DiskMap</name>
    <summary>See where your storage is going — treemap and top consumers, instance-wide</summary>
    <description><![CDATA[
DiskMap shows where storage is going across your Nextcloud instance — per user and per team
folder — without scanning anything.

Nextcloud already tracks aggregated folder sizes in its file cache, updated on every operation.
DiskMap is a visualizer over data that already exists: it never triggers a filesystem scan.

Each view pairs a WinDirStat-style treemap with an expandable folder tree, kept in sync both
ways: click a tile on the map and the tree opens to that file, click a row in the tree and the
map highlights its region.

**For administrators:**
- Whole-server view: every account, team folder and external storage as a top-level entry,
  browsable down to individual files.
- Team folders overview: used space, quota and occupancy, with a files / trash / versions
  breakdown for each folder.

**For every user:**
- The same treemap and folder tree over your own storage, with quota occupancy and a
  files / trash / versions breakdown.

All figures show the timestamp of the underlying file cache entry, so it's always clear this
reflects what Nextcloud's cache knows, not a live disk read.
    ]]></description>
    <version>0.1.0</version>
    <licence>AGPL-3.0-or-later</licence>
    <author mail="rsfneg@gmail.com">Ricardo Ferreira</author>
    <namespace>DiskMap</namespace>
    <documentation>
        <admin>https://github.com/kreotropic/diskmap#usage</admin>
    </documentation>
    <category>tools</category>
    <category>monitoring</category>
    <website>https://github.com/kreotropic/diskmap</website>
    <bugs>https://github.com/kreotropic/diskmap/issues</bugs>
    <repository type="git">https://github.com/kreotropic/diskmap.git</repository>

    <!-- The App Store renders only these URLs; it does not crawl the README
         for images, and screenshots/ is excluded from the release tarball
         (.nextcloudignore), so they have to be absolute https URLs served
         from the repository. -->
    <screenshot>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kreotropic/diskmap/main/screenshots/1-whole-server.png</screenshot>
    <screenshot>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kreotropic/diskmap/main/screenshots/2-my-storage.png</screenshot>
    <screenshot>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kreotropic/diskmap/main/screenshots/3-team-folder.png</screenshot>
    <screenshot>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kreotropic/diskmap/main/screenshots/4-tree-map-sync.png</screenshot>

    <dependencies>
        <php min-version="8.1"/>
        <!-- The composition queries are the app's only raw SQL and its only
             dialect-dependent surface; FilecacheUsageSource::isPostgres()
             documents what differs. SQLite is deliberately still excluded:
             it needs a third spelling of the same path-segment expression and
             has no coverage, so declaring only what is tested keeps the app
             off instances where every view would 500. -->
        <!-- sqlite added ONLY for the Nextcloud Playground demo: the browser
             runtime installs against SQLite, and without a matching <database>
             entry occ app:enable refuses even when forced. Composition and
             file-count queries stay MySQL/PostgreSQL-only, so those two
             columns are blank in the Playground; everything else works. -->
        <database>sqlite</database>
        <database>mysql</database>
        <database>pgsql</database>
        <nextcloud min-version="32" max-version="34"/>
    </dependencies>

    <navigations>
        <navigation>
            <name>DiskMap</name>
            <route>diskmap.page.index</route>
            <icon>app.svg</icon>
        </navigation>
    </navigations>
</info>
